scope: Measure the installed GTK2 DomainOS scrollbar allocations and GtkScrolledWindow frame gap against the SR10.4 VUE contract, then probe the contract value without changing the user profile.

runtime.session: lsi desktop XWayland DISPLAY=:1; isolated native GTK2 preview fixture
runtime.scale: 1:1; XWD capture and lossless PNG conversion

scanline_gap.measurement: Count face pixels between the two-pixel outer scrolled-content bevel and the scrollbar trough bevel; horizontal and vertical scans agree.

endpoint_cells.gtk2_spacing4_probe: same direct and best pixel differences as spacing 3; increasing the frame gap did not move the stepper artwork to the allocated scrollbar edges.

probe.result: The GTK2 style property read back as 4. At fixed outer allocation 557x273, H/V allocations reduce by one pixel to 538x15 and 15x254; the visual face gap becomes 4 px. This probe did not change the GTK2 color roles or stepper assets.

limits: The GtkTreeView has a real scroll range and therefore a shorter thumb than the empty VUE Trash Can; full-track pixel percentages are not used as an appearance metric.
Normal state only. No guest input, live profile change, app restart, or scheme switch.
The spacing probe confirms the four-pixel gap but does not resolve the 2-pixel endpoint placement. I517 remains a separate authorization for direct guest input.
result: The actual GTK2 GtkScrolledWindow uses a 3px spacing default, while the SR10.4 contract measures 4px between the content-frame bevel and scrollbar. A private style override to 4px reproduces that gap exactly. The endpoint 15x15 cells still match the VUE artwork only after independent +/-2px translation; therefore spacing and endpoint placement are separate corrections.
